features.title: Feed ordered by activity, with idle items sinking
features.summary: The feed lists pinned items, then activity in chronological order with newest at bottom beside the composer. Each entry's activity line names the actor of its last change and links an Agent to the thread it worked in. Status chips narrow the feed and the Items list to one status or several at once. From an empty capture box, ArrowUp focuses the nearest visible item and arrow keys follow the list's visual order. Freshness is derived on read: notes go dormant after 14 days, other open items after 30, idle in-progress work is flagged stale, closed items archive after 7 days; any touch revives an item. The open panel stays current from the Host's `changed` event (a write, delete or peer pull re-reads the revision at once); without the event it polls the revision every 5 s, and only while it is visible.
failureModes: Dormant and archived items stay in search and backlinks; only the default feed hides them.

features.title: Triage new items automatically

features.title: Start a thread from an item
features.summary: Clicking a board card opens the item detail beside the board. Right-clicking an item in the feed, Inbox, Items, Board, Projects, search results, or its detail view opens the same actions: start a linked thread; copy the item ID or its clickable `b:<id>` reference; change status, kind, attention or project; pin or unpin; run triage when Jev or a triage model is configured; or open the item. Starting a thread picks the item project, account/model and effort, and an opening message; the row selected in the Items table starts a thread for the whole selection, every item is linked and named in the opening message, and the thread is created in its own jj workspace of that project, named and linked. The Host adds every full item description and current reply in order, with every item and reply attachment; missing, unreadable or oversized context fails rather than silently omitting it, and upload or prompt failure reports the created Session id. The dialog closes as soon as it hands the request over, so the panel never waits for the workspace; the banner says the work is under way, the thread opens only when the startThreadOpensCreated setting asks for it, or when the dialog's open box overrides it for one thread; an @agent comment follows the same setting, and the report carries an Open action otherwise. The Host verb behind it is the tool `backlog_start_thread`, which does not navigate the calling thread.

features.title: Mirror backlog items in Linear, GitHub Issues, markdown files or a plugin provider
features.summary: Link an item to a remote item through any binding that serves its project, create one from it, or unlink it from its row menu or its sync chips in the item detail; an item may be linked through several bindings, one chip each. Each binding's field map decides which of title, description, status, labels, priority, parent and relations flow which way, with remote status names mapped per status; a field both sides changed is settled by the binding's conflict policy (last change wins, backlog wins, remote wins, or flag) with a conflict note on the item. Statuses compare by equivalence so an item in progress stays in progress against an open GitHub issue. A binding pass pulls what changed since its cursor (Linear updatedAt pages, GitHub since= with ETags, a full scan of a markdown folder), writes remote changes as remote:<bindingId> ops, pushes local changes, carries new comments once each way when the provider supports them, drops items whose remote file is gone, and can import every open remote item. Agents read the same state with backlog_sync_status and act with backlog_sync_now, backlog_link_remote and backlog_sync_import_all when the user asked. Comments agents write stay local unless the binding pushes them.

features.title: Agents claim items with a lease; you release them
features.summary: backlog_claim hands an item to the calling agent thread in one write: it becomes the delegate (the owner stays whoever captured it), moves to In progress, links the thread and starts a lease. The inspector shows Owner · Delegate and the claim with a Release action; rows and cards show a lock chip. `is:claimed`, `is:delegated` and `delegate:agent` search them. features.title: Wait on a PR, a revision, a check or a date, and see linked PRs live
features.currentSurface: left-nav: Backlog › item detail › Waits on, Pull requests
features.summary: Gates hold an item out of the ready queue until a pull request merges, a jj revision lands on main, a project check passes in a thread linked to the item, or a date arrives (is:gated, has:gate, a chip on rows and cards). A Host gate watch resolves them on the revision poll cadence from the pull-requests contract, one jj read per repository and project-check receipts; a date gate follows the calendar. GitHub pull and GitLab merge-request URLs are PR links: Link PR in the detail or backlog_link_pr links one as fixes and asks pull-requests to watch it through the item's newest thread; the detail and backlog_pull_requests show open, merged or closed and checks, and a fixing PR that merges closes its item unless its status was set by hand. Without the pull-requests plugin they stay plain URLs.
failureModes: Without the pull-requests plugin, PR gates never resolve on their own and PR links show as plain links; remove the gate or install the plugin.

features.title: Share one backlog across Hosts
features.summary: Every Host serves its op log read-only to peers (peerInfo, peerOpsSince after a cursor, peerFiles) and pulls each multi-host runtime turned on in Backlog settings › Hosts every peerPullSeconds, or now with Sync now or backlog_peer_sync. A Host serves every op it holds, so A ↔ B ↔ C converges; ingest skips ops it has and folds only the touched items in one total order; an offline Host is skipped and caught up from its cursor. Another Host's item gets a private local number; a ref two Hosts minted stays on the older item and the newer gets a derived ref with a note; another Host's legacy item shows under a derived ref that resolves on both; merge redirects travel as ops; a recurring item finished on two Hosts spawns one next occurrence. Attachment bytes come from a peer when an item is opened, or ahead after each pass, kept only when they match their SHA-256. Gate checks and main polling run only on the chosen automation Host. The section lists each runtime with a switch, last pull, ops to pull, its error and Sync now, and the automation Host picker; the work log names the Host that wrote an event. Agents read backlog_peer_status and, when the user asked, call backlog_peer_sync and backlog_peers_configure.

configuration.constraints: Hidden; { runtimeId, enabled } per multi-host runtime, edited in Backlog settings › Hosts or with backlog_peers_configure. Off by default: nothing is pulled until a runtime is turned on.
10 to 3600 seconds between pulls of every enabled peer.
Hidden; the backlog Host id that runs gate checks and main polling. Empty: this Host (with a note asking to pick one once peers are on).

failureModes: Without @dshfiles/multi-host the section says the backlog stays on this Host and nothing pulls.
An offline or unreachable Host is skipped with its error and caught up from its saved cursor on a later pull.
A Host on another peer protocol or a newer op schema is refused before anything is stored, with what to update (Hosts panel › Update hosts, or multi_host_update) and a restart.
A Host without the backlog plugin answers api-not-served; the row asks to enable it there or turn the peer off.
An op that does not decode with this Host's op schema stops the pull and stores nothing of that page.
Attachment bytes that do not hash to their SHA-256 are refused and asked from the next peer.
With peers on and no automation Host picked, every Host still runs gate checks and main polling and the section asks to pick one.
A Host that predates backlog Hosts answers without the methods; the section asks for a DSH Host process restart.
